## What he talks about most

Counted across the sermon (± 4,400 words): **God** comes up 98 times and the words for **living, life and lives** 79 times. Then the **forgive** family **40×**, **see/sees/seen 38×**, **heart 28×**, **pain, hurt and wound 24×**, **wholeheartedly 23×**, **unforgiveness 22×**, **freedom 22×**, **darkness 20×** against **light 18×**, **fullness 17×**, **trust 14×** and **debt 10×**. "Grace" appears 7 times, and it carries the whole thing.

That is the sermon in one count: the life God intends is a full one, lived with your whole heart — and what most quietly blocks it is a wound you never dealt with. He preaches in images you can hold: a pitch-dark cabin, a gunshot, a cancelled debt, a hidden cupboard.

## The one point he wants to make

**Unforgiveness costs you far more than it costs the person who hurt you. Forgiveness is not letting them off; it is how you get your own heart back.**

> "Forgiveness will free you. Unforgiveness will imprison you." (1:09:29)

The title comes from Numbers 14:24, where God says of Caleb that he *"has a different spirit and follows me wholeheartedly"* (51:49). The subtitle he gives it himself: living in the fullness of forgiveness, free from the pain of the past (52:30).

## The foundation: how do you see God?

Before a word about forgiving anyone, he lays the foundation: *"the key to this, I believe, is founded in how you see God"* (53:56). Back in the garden the enemy's first move was a question, not an attack: did God really say that? He tells it through a cabin in the middle of nowhere, where he got up at night and felt his way through the dark.

> "Amsterdam dark is grey, but when there's no cities around, when there's no lights around, dark is dark, you can't see in front of you." (56:16)

That is the dominion of darkness: *"a spiritual darkness where you can't see the truth about God, you can't see the truth about yourself"* (56:49) — the dark in which you measure your worth by your performance or by other people's opinion. Against it he sets Colossians 1:12–14: the Father has qualified you and brought you into the kingdom of light. *"You are fully seen, fully known, fully loved... he delights in you"* (58:01).

## The cost, and whose job the wound is

*"The price of unforgiveness, guys, is just too high"* (1:02:05) — not because the other person gets away with it, but because of what it does inside you.

> "You may be wounded once, but unforgiveness can make you just relive it a thousand times." (1:02:42)

It keeps you tied to the one who hurt you: *"they live in your heart rent free"* (1:03:17). Replaying it and suppressing it both hand that person influence over your thoughts, emotions and future.

Then the turn of the sermon, made with himself in the picture rather than us: someone shoots me, and I can spend my life saying he shot me, it wasn't right, there needs to be justice — all of it true.

> "What has happened to you may not be your fault, but what you do with it is your responsibility." (1:04:33)

*"However, if I don't take responsibility for my wound, I'll bleed out and die"* (1:05:07). He blames no one for being wounded; the healing is the part that is ours. And the trap: *"I think I'm making them pay. But I'm the one paying the price"* (1:06:23).

## The debt, the king and the jailer

Matthew 18: Peter asks how often he must forgive; Jesus answers with a king, a servant whose debt is beyond a lifetime's wages, and that servant refusing a far smaller one. The ending — handed over to the jailers — he reads as how life works rather than as a threat: *"he set up life that we would live in freedom, that we would live in grace, that we would live in forgiveness"* (1:08:16).

> "Hurt people hurt people... until the cycle stops. And we're called to be those people." (1:08:55)

Then he clears the misunderstandings away (1:10:07): forgiveness is not saying it was okay, not forgetting, not reconciliation, not trusting again, not denying justice. It is: *"I acknowledge what happened. I acknowledge that it hurt. I acknowledge there was a debt. But I choose not to carry that debt anymore."* And: *"You forgive not because they deserve freedom. You forgive because you deserve freedom."*

## Out of the cupboard, into the light

What if you cannot even find it? *"It's like we find some hidden storage cupboard in our heart that no one's ever going to find, that we won't even find, because we don't want to deal with that pain"* (1:11:55). His verdict on that strategy is one line: **"Hiding it doesn't mean it's healed."**

How do you know something is still there? By what sets you off today — a tender place that flares up, being told as a child you were dumb or ugly, a rejection, a failure (1:13:35). What blocks you from honouring God with your relationships, words or finances is often not unwillingness but something unhealed you are protecting. And the reassurance alongside the invitation: *"when you bring it into the light, God doesn't shame you"* (1:12:27).

## What he has had to forgive himself

He does not preach this from above. He has prayed for others and seen healing and breakthrough — *"and yet for years I've prayed for myself and [my wife] to have children, and we haven't seen a miracle there"* (1:16:53). That turned the question back on him: can I really trust God with everything? His answer is not an explanation but a Person: God's nature and character. *"Sometimes we see a part. He sees fully"* (1:17:58), like the farmer in the old Chinese fable who keeps answering *"good luck, bad luck, who knows?"* (1:18:30).

Then the specifics, without naming anyone: unfair treatment, being passed over by people of authority close to him, deep betrayals (1:19:36–1:20:12). *"But I choose to live with a freedom of heart."* He closes with Psalm 139 — search me, know my heart — at a gentle pace: *"it's one step at a time"* (1:22:28).

## Scriptures for further reading

| Text | In the sermon | For further reading |
|---|---|---|
| Num. 14:24 | Caleb follows God wholeheartedly and receives the land | Read Numbers 13–14: ten spies see giants, two see God. Caleb tells it himself in Josh. 14:6–14, still strong at 85. The same wholeheartedness lands on ordinary work in **Col. 3:23**. |
| Gen. 3:1–5 · John 10:10 | "did God really say?"; the thief steals, Jesus gives life to the full | The doubt targets God's intention, not the rule (**2 Cor. 11:3**). In John 10:1–18 the fullness hangs on a shepherd who lays down his life. |
| Col. 1:12–14 · Prov. 4:23 | rescued from the dominion of darkness; guard your heart | The same move out of darkness: **Acts 26:18**, **1 Pet. 2:9**. Prov. 4:20–27 sets heart, mouth, eyes and feet as one whole. |
| Matt. 18:21–35 | the king, the unpayable debt, the jailers | 10,000 talents against 100 denarii — a lifetime against a day's wage. Shorter versions: **Mark 11:25**, **Luke 17:3–4**, prayed in **Matt. 6:12, 14–15**. |
| Col. 3:13 · Eph. 4:26–27 | forgive as the Lord forgave you; give the devil no foothold | The parallel is **Eph. 4:31–32**; **Heb. 12:15** names the same danger, a bitter root that grows and defiles many. |
| Luke 4:18–19 | freedom for prisoners, the year of the Lord's favour | Jesus reads **Isa. 61:1–2**; Luke 4:16–21 tells what follows. |
| Ps. 139:23–24 · Phil. 4:4–7 | search me, God; rejoice, and God's peace will guard your heart (1:32:46) | The searching is asked of the God who already knows every word (v. 1–4); its echo is **1 John 1:7, 9**. Phil. 4 follows an appeal to two people in conflict (4:2–3). |

**Grace first.** Forgiving is never put here as a performance you owe. He gives the order plainly: *"we forgive because we've already been forgiven. We receive grace and we give that grace. We are loved and we give that love. God starts this"* (1:01:33). That is exactly Colossians 3:13 and Ephesians 4:32 — the "as" comes before the "so". And he leaves room for anyone not there yet: one step at a time, only what you can handle today.

## From the rest of the service

- **Prayer for the church family** (27:25): out loud for healing, provision, a home, pregnancies, a returning brain tumour, and for those mourning.
- **Offering** (42:47): Prov. 4:23 and Rom. 12:1–2 from The Message — the heart drifts first and the actions follow, so *"we wait for our hearts to change for us to start serving again"* (44:33). Sometimes it is simply a decision, and the heart follows after.
- **Back from sabbatical**; next week the speaker is with the Rotterdam location, which celebrates 10 years (50:30).
- **Coming up:** Sisterhood One Day on Sat 26 Sep (35:14) · Youth night on 9 Oct (38:35) · Hillsong Conference in London at the end of October (39:45).
- **Altar call** (1:35:43): hands raised across the room and a prayer prayed together — *"my past will not determine my future, but my relationship with you will"* (1:38:07).

## One line to listen for

**What was done to you may not be your fault, but the wound is yours to get healed — and you forgive not because they deserve freedom, but because you do.**
